'''Ama Kazukime Shrine''' (海士潜女神社, Ama Kazukime Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] located in [[Kuzakichō]], [[Toba, Mie|Toba City]], [[Mie Prefecture]]. It was formerly known as Ama Gozen (海士御前) until 1869. While not under the administration of [[Ise Grand Shrine]], it maintains a deep connection to Ise and enshrines the legendary [[ama (female diver)|Ama diver]] Oben, attracting faith from divers across Japan.
Ama Kazukime Shrine enshrines the legendary ama named Oben, who dedicated an abalone to Emperor's Princess, Yamatohime-no-mikoto. The shrine is regarded as having divine favor in preventing dizziness during diving and is worshiped by local amas and divers nation-wide.<ref>https://www.bing.com/ck/a?!&&p=5de8780f388380bac94109889b3b4851fbe31c06bec1a4e2bc67168448801156JmltdHM9MTc0MzYzODQwMA&ptn=3&ver=2&hsh=4&fclid=0baff627-1adb-6b49-298a-e3e31b796a0d&u=a1aHR0cHM6Ly9xcnRyYW5zbGF0b3IuY29tLzAwMDAwMDE3NDcvMDAwMDAx&ntb=1</ref>
== Overview ==
The [[Honden|honden]] of the shrine is a wooden structure in [[Shinmei-zukuri]], while the [[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]] is built in [[Nagare-zukuri]] and surrounded by [[sacred fences]]. The grounds span approximately 920 [[Pyeong|tsubo]] (about 3,041 square meters). The main deity is Kazukime-no-Kami, identified with the legendary ama Oben. She is revered as the progenitor of ama divers, offering protection against dizziness and marine hazards. The shrine is also a pilgrimage site for divers across Japan.
== History ==
In the 26th year of Emperor [[Emperor Suinin|Suinin]] (4 BCE), [[Yamatohime-no-mikoto]] visited Kuzaki while searching for offerings for the [[Ise Grand Shrine]]. Oben presented abalone, which impressed Yamatohime and was subsequently dedicated to Ise. This marked Kuzaki’s selection as one of Ise’s [[Kanbe (social class)|Divine rice fields]]. The shrine was renamed Ama Kazukime Shrine in 1869 and later consolidated 17 smaller shrines between 1906 and 1907.
== Rituals ==
=== Hachiman Festival ===
Originally the festival of Hachiman Shrine, it centers around archery rituals held on [[January 5]]. Key rituals include the "Manabashi" ceremony, where chosen men prepare fish with chopsticks and knives without touching it by hand.
=== Two Boat Festival ===
Held annually over three days in November, this festival involves competitive boat races between the Kuzaki subregions of Satodani and Kaimadani. Participants offer fish and [[Omiki|omiki]] at the [[Shinto shrine]] during the race, believed to predict the year’s fishing fortune.
=== Mikazuki Ritual and Grand Festival===
Historically, this ritual involved female divers from seven villages gathering on the lunar calendar's June 1 to dive for abalone. Although discontinued in 1871, the ritual has been periodically revived for commemorative occasions, such as the 2016 G7 Ise-Shima Summit.

== Subsidiary Shrines Enshrined Together ==
The Amamochime Shrine enshrines the following 17 shrines, which were merged into it in 1906 and 1907. All of these shrines originally held no specific Rank under the [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]].<ref name="th3">Toba City History Compilation Office (1991): pp. 980–982.</ref>

=== Tsurugi-no-Miya Shrine ===
Tsurugi-no-Miya Shrine (剱宮社) was originally located on Tsurugi Cape. It was merged into Amamochime Shrine in 1906 (Meiji 39). It is also known simply as Tsurugi Shrine.<ref name="kk4"/> According to legend, one of the [[Imperial Regalia of Japan|Three Sacred Treasures]], the [[Kusanagi no Tsurugi|Kusanagi Sword]], which sank during the [[Battle of Dan-no-ura]] alongside Emperor Antoku, was retrieved from the sea by a monk named Ajari Enjo and subsequently enshrined there.<ref name="kk4"/>
== Festivals ==
Amamochime Shrine is home to two major festivals in Kunisaki Town: the Hachiman Festival and the Two Boats Festival.<ref name="sg63">Shimamoto (1994): p. 163.</ref>
=== Hachiman Festival ===
Originally dedicated to the Hachiman Shrine, this festival centers around an archery ritual held on January 5th.<ref name="sg63"/> Hachiman Festivals are widely celebrated in fishing villages across Toba City, emphasizing prayers for bountiful catches and maritime safety.<ref>Toba City History Compilation Office (1991): p. 809.</ref> 
The festival includes:
* '''"Hatsuyori" (January 2nd):''' Preparatory meetings for the archery ritual.<ref name="sg63"/>
* '''"Daikon Kaki" (January 4th):''' Households prepare the offerings for the next day.<ref name="sg63"/>
During the festival, participants perform the [[Manabashi Ritual]], in which fish is filleted into sashimi using chopsticks and knives without touching it by hand.<ref name="th9">Toba City History Compilation Office (1991): p. 809.</ref>
=== Two Boats Festival ===
The Two Boats Festival (二船祭) takes place over three days in November.<ref name="tt">Toba Tourism Association "[http://www.toba.gr.jp/200/post_523.html Two Boats Festival]" <[https://megalodon.jp/2013-0421-1742-58/www.toba.gr.jp/200/post_523.html Web Archive]> (accessed April 21, 2013).</ref> The highlight is a boat race between the Kaima and Satodani communities, representing prayers for abundant fish catches.<ref name="sg63"/> 
== Surroundings ==
The shrine is located in Kunisaki Town, near the center of Toba City. Visitors can take the Kamome Bus from the [[Sangū Line|JR Sangu Line]] Toba Station to the Kunisaki stop, followed by a 7-minute walk.<ref name="cv"/> Note that there is no dedicated parking space nearby.<ref name="cv"/>
